messages:
Maya: Heads up — customers on mistral-lite-v3 are reporting higher p95/p99 for long conversations after the tokenizer update we rolled earlier today. Seeing lots of SLA complaints.
Alex: Can you paste one of the slow traces and a sample request? Which endpoints (generate/chat/embeddings)?
Maya: generate, long prompts (~12k-25k tokens). From the dashboard: baseline p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. After rollout p95 ~340ms, p99 ~1.1s for >12k token requests. Small prompts unaffected. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/XYz12 (private)
Juniper: Noticed a spike in KV-cache miss rate concurrent with rollout. Metric kv_cache_miss_ratio jumped from 0.7% -> 9.8% for sessions using v3 tokenizer.
Sam: Stack traces show extra token expansion during pre-tokenization stage — looks like the new merge heuristic is producing more subword tokens for CJK-heavy inputs. Example diff: old tokens 9,800 -> new tokens 11,400 for same input.
Luis: Repro steps I used: 
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-lite-v3","input":"<very long conversation>" , "max_tokens":1024}' -w "\\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}s\\n"
```
Response: TIME_TOTAL:1.12s (after rollout). Before rollout same request TIME_TOTAL:0.32s.
Maya: Also seeing queue growth on the CPU tokenizer worker pods -> bursts of backpressure before requests hit GPUs.
Alex: Hypothesis: tokenizer change increases token count + changes token boundaries causing more KV cache fragmentation -> less reuse of past keys -> more compute per request and higher latency tails. Also batching behavior may degrade because sequence-length distribution widened.
Juniper: I pulled a few raw request traces. Example: 
```
Request id: r-83321
input_tokens: old=9800 new=11400
kv_cache_hits: 88% -> 74%
cpu_tokenize_ms: 45ms -> 180ms
server_total_ms: 320ms -> 1120ms
```
Sam: Thank you. That matches. For CJK and emoji-heavy messages the token multiplier is worst. We need to both mitigate customer impact and fix the tokenizer.
Alex: Immediate mitigations we can roll now: 
- Pin model alias to a legacy tokenizer build (mistral-lite-v3:tkn-legacy) for the hosted model pool.
- Temporarily disable the new tokenizer heuristic via feature flag (tokenizer.enable_merge_heuristic=false).
- Reduce max_batch_size and lower batching_window_ms to reduce head-of-line queuing for long sequences.
- Add a request-level soft limit: if input_tokens > 10k, return a friendly 429-like guidance or route to dedicated pool.

Juniper: I kicked a canary rollback for 5% traffic to the legacy tokenizer alias. Observed p99 back to ~410ms on canary.
Maya: Which API call do we use to change alias? I can apply to affected customers.
Luis: Admin snippet (internal):
```
POST /internal/admin/models/aliases
{
  "model": "mistral-lite-v3",
  "alias": "default",
  "target": "mistral-lite-v3:tkn-legacy",
  "force": true
}
```
Alex: I created a PR to flip the feature flag and add a short-circuit path that preserves prior tokenization for sessions started before rollout: GH#4123. Planning to merge after one more approval.
SRE-bot: ALERT: Tokenizer-Worker-CPU OOMs increased by 3x on prod clusters in us-west-2 between 1723452000 and 1723458000.
Sam: Longer term: revert or patch the merge heuristic to respect a max expansion ratio, add regression tests in the tokenization eval harness (include CJK/emoji/long-dialog fixtures), and add a canary stage for tokenizer changes with synthetic long-sequence traffic.
Juniper: Ops checklist I'm doing now:
- Scale tokenizer worker pool + autoscale config
- Apply alias rollback to affected hosted models
- Lower global batching window to 8ms for 30m
- Add a telemetry gate for token expansion >1.15x per request to alert faster

Maya: I've informed the top 3 affected customers and offered temporary pinning. Support ticket numbers: SUP-8213, SUP-8214. Customers accepted pin to legacy tokenizer for now.
Alex: Next actions:
1) Merge PR GH#4123 to flip feature flag (in progress).
2) Keep canary at 5% for 30m -> monitor p95/p99 and kv_cache_hit.
3) Run token expansion job across model zoo and generate list of high-risk locales.
4) Add regression test and hold release until we have a baseline for long-context.

Luis: I'll create a short runbook note under internal runbooks/tokenizer-longseq.md with commands to pin aliases and check kv cache metrics.
Maya: I'll close the customer tickets once rollback verification completes.
Alex: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread and paste any new slow traces. :thumbsup:
